candidates.title: File:Fresco of Baba Gurbaksh Singh Shaheed from Gurdwara Baba Atal in Amritsar.jpg
candidates.author: Painted by Gian Singh Naqqash, Jaimal Singh Naqqash (1860–1916), Mehtab Singh Naqqash (1871–1940), and Hukum Singh. The word 'Naqqash' means 'artist'. Originally the work had been done by several artists during Sikh-rule.
candidates.description: Fresco of Baba Gurbaksh Singh Shaheed from Gurdwara Baba Atal in Amritsar. The frescoes of Gurdwara Baba Atal are believed to have been originally painted around the mid-to-late-19th century (though photographer and author Satpal Danish, whom wrote a book on the frescoes, claims they were originally created during Sikh-rule), using Indian red, ochre and other earth colours with gold accents. However, almost all were repainted in a 1971 "renovation" in a very garish manner using artificial colouring and synthetic paint. Many of these frescoes have been destroyed, defaced, or deteriorated through neglect and harmful "renovations" since they were documented in photographs, especially on the ground floor during "kar seva" (renovations) in the 1990's. Description from: [1] (which dates the painting to the 18th century but that seems unlikely, it is probably from the 19th century) Akali Nihang Singh Khalsa: A old painting of Akali Nihang Baba Gurbux Singh c.1700s, holding a 'salotar' (a heavy wooden club) also known as an 'Akal-dhaan' (bringer of wisdom)

candidates.title: File:Fresco depicting the body of Guru Nanak as his family and followers stand around him - Baba Atal, Amritsar.jpg
candidates.author: Usingh0663
candidates.description: Depicts of a somber crowd of the first Guru of Sikhism, Guru Nanak, and his Family and Followers mourning his death. This fresco is from the Baba Atal Gurudwara in Amritsar. The gurmukhi inscriptions describe the scene and name the various attendants.

candidates.title: File:Gilded panel depicting bhagat Dhanna the Jat and his life-story (sakhi) from Gurdwara Baba Atal Rai, Amritsar, ca.1904.jpg
candidates.author: Gilded panel made by the craftsmen of Kucha Fakirkhana. Photographed by T.S. Randhawa.
candidates.credit: Twitter thread by user @moomjamma, via: link
candidates.description: Gilded panel depicting bhagat Dhanna the Jat and his life-story (sakhi) from Gurdwara Baba Atal Rai, Amritsar. Gilded Panel, embossed brass, plated in gold, made by the craftsmen of Kucha Fakirkhana, Amritsar in 1904. Photographed by T.S. Randhawa. "The panel shows various scenes from the famous Sakhi of Dhanna and the 'Thakaar' (idol) given to him by a Brahmin. In the sakhi Dhanna asks a brahmin for an idol, he gives him a four 'ser' weight stone in exchange for a milch cow. Dhanna performs such devoted service to the ‘Thakaar’ that the ‘Formless One’ takes form and appears. In the panel you can see Dhanna and the Brahmin, Dhanna and his wife. You also see ‘Thaakar’ working the 'Halt' (Persian wheel irrigation), working the fields ( kiare khaddan ) and the tools of a Jat farmer." (description taken from source) "Another plaque illustrates Lord Krishna and Saint Dhanna, which was, according to its inscription, dedicated by Lal Chand Kandhri, son of Bhag Mal Kandhri." (quote taken from: link ) The tale (from: [1] ; [2] ): "Dhanna ji worshipping a Shaligram, leading to the manifestation of Narayan in the form of Chaturbhuja Chakradhari. He hailed from a Hindu Jat family of Dhaliwal gotra in Chauru village of Tehsil Phagi, Jaipur. Bhakt Dhanna was a devoted disciple of the Vaishnava Bhakti Saint poet Guru Shri Ramananda ji, the founder of the Ramanandi Sampradaya. Through his offerings of Chaas and Roti to Shaligram ji, Bhakt Dhanna's unwavering devotion pleased Bhagwan Vishnu, resulting in his divine manifestation before him. Bhakt Dhanna Jat receives a Shaligram from a Thakurdwara. In order to procure food items for God, Dhanna Bhagat went to the market and sold his seeds. To avoid his parents' disapproval, he pretended to sow the seeds in the field by ploughing and watering it. Much to Dhanna Bhagat's astonishment, the seedless field miraculously yielded a lush and healthy crop of wheat, thanks to the grace of God. Chakradhari Narayan, in his Chaturbhuj form, assists him in the fields."
